title: Turnout and issue estimates take the sign of the ad's valence
location: published pp. 10 to 11, Figure 4; appendix Tables C.3 to C.5, C.8 to C.10, and C.13 to C.15
published: The slopes of all four meta-regression lines are close to zero and are not statistically significant.
note: The sentence survives, and the numbers behind it do not. `estimate_all_cates.R` multiplies every outcome by -1 for an anti ad, which suits candidate favorability and vote choice. It also flips turnout, so an anti ad that raises turnout plots as lowering it, in 90 of 102 estimates. For issues the deposit's `ad_id_to_base_by_hand.csv` carries a `direction` column that no script reads, and it disagrees with the sign used in 63 of 102 estimates. Without the turnout flip and with `direction` on issues, Figure 4's labels change: on turnout, -0.017 (0.021) becomes 0.017 (0.021) and 0.064 (0.035) becomes -0.052 (0.028); on issues, 0.052 (0.059) becomes 0.018 (0.072) and -0.039 (0.041) becomes -0.053 (0.042). All four remain indistinguishable from zero. An ad might be meant to demobilize, so the article's text cannot settle the intended sign on turnout, and this item corrects nothing.

title: Three attack ads are coded positive
published: If an ad’s purpose was to attack an opponent, we code it as negative in tone, regardless of the colors or sounds it uses
note: Table D.16 codes the anti-Trump ads “America's Bullies”, “Example”, and “Families” as positive.
